author: west la times
title: UCLA women's basketball falls short against No.4 Texas at Players Era Championship - West LA Times
text:
The UCLA women’s basketball team, ranked third nationally, was defeated by No. 4 Texas with a score of 76-65 during the opening game of the Players Era Women’s Championship held at Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas on Wednesday.
UCLA (6-1) fell behind early and trailed Texas (6-0) by 20 points at halftime, with the score standing at 45-25. Despite narrowing the deficit to four points late in the game, UCLA was unable to overtake Texas.
Senior Kiki Rice and graduate student Gianna Kneepkens each contributed 17 points for UCLA. Rice also collected six rebounds and three assists, while Kneepkens added two rebounds and two assists. Graduate student Charlisse Leger-Walker scored 13 points along with three rebounds and two assists.
For Texas, Rori Harmon led all scorers with 26 points, making both her three-point attempts and converting all six free throws. Harmon also recorded three rebounds and five assists as one of four Longhorns to reach double figures in scoring.
Texas established control early after gaining a two-point lead less than two minutes into the first quarter. A 10-2 run by Texas closed out the opening period, giving them a ten-point advantage heading into the second quarter.
The Longhorns extended their lead further in the second quarter by outscoring UCLA 25-15. Turnovers were a significant issue for UCLA in the first half; they committed ten compared to just one by Texas. The Bruins did not score any points off turnovers during this stretch, while Texas managed twelve.
Texas made three of eight shots from beyond the arc in the first half and finished shooting 43.5 percent from the field overall (27-for-62). UCLA ended up shooting slightly better at 47.1 percent against their opponent.
Kneepkens scored ten of her seventeen points during a strong third-quarter performance where she went four-for-four from the field including two three-pointers. Late in that period, Angela Dugalić capitalized on a turnover by feeding Kneepkens for another successful shot from distance following back-to-back free throws from Rice.
UCLA outscored Texas 22-17 in the third quarter while shooting over fifty-three percent compared to thirty-three percent for Texas but still trailed by fifteen entering the fourth quarter.
In the final period, Kneepkens hit an early three-pointer then forced a turnover leading to an assist on a basket by Dugalić that prompted a timeout from Texas. After both teams went through a scoring drought at 54-64, Rice scored consecutive layups—one assisted by Lauren Betts—to cut Texas’ lead to four before another timeout was called. However, UCLA failed to convert any field goals over their last five attempts across more than four minutes as time expired.
Turnovers continued to be problematic for UCLA throughout; they finished with twenty compared to ten for Texas. The Longhorns also led statistically in blocks (5-2), steals (9-6), and assists (16-12). Both teams performed well at the free throw line: UCLA shot nearly ninety-three percent while Texas converted over ninety-four percent of their attempts; however, Texas had an edge from long range making forty percent compared to thirty-one percent for UCLA.
UCLA will next play Duke University on Thursday, November 27th at 7:30 p.m., with coverage available on truTV and HBO Max.
